# Smooth subgroup generated by local graphs

Author: Worker 1444.

This internal derived construction implements the generated subgroup in the
graph argument of Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), 23.17–23.18, printed
pp.490–491 (PDF pp.506–507). It reuses the published
`FiniteGeneration.exists_smooth_generated_family` construction rather than
assuming a generated representative or reimplementing its existence proof.

Over any field `k : Type u`, take smooth affine group schemes `G₁` and
`G₂`, a smooth connected affine group scheme `T`, and maps `i₁ : T → G₁`
and `i₂ : T → G₂`. Take an arbitrary family `A j` of smooth connected
affine group schemes, indexed by an independent `I : Type v`, with maps
`a₁ j : A j → G₁` and `a₂ j : A j → G₂`.

`graphEnvelope` constructs an actual smooth connected affine group scheme
`D` with a closed inclusion into `G₁ × G₂`. This subgroup contains the
paired maps `(a₁ j, a₂ j)` and `(i₁, i₂)`, and is minimal among all closed
subgroups containing them. Its minimality is a containment of subgroup
functors on every test scheme; competitors need not be smooth or reduced.
The ambient groups need not be connected or reductive. The input maps need
not be embeddings, and `T` need not be commutative. The constructor obtains
smoothness and affineness of the ambient product from the two factors and
then applies the arbitrary-family theorem to a family indexed by `Option I`.
The `none` generator is `T`; this ensures that its lift exists even for an
empty local family.

The record `GraphEnvelope` retains this geometry and generation property.
Its `first` and `second` maps are the two actual group-scheme projections.
`generatorLift`, `localLift` and `torusLift` are actual group homomorphisms
obtained from the represented range of the closed inclusion. Their displayed
equations identify both projections. `points_ext` and `hom_ext` prove joint
injectivity on every test scheme by monomorphy of the inclusion and the
product universal property. Consequently any local map from `T` whose
two projections agree with `i₁` and `i₂` gives the distinguished
`torusLift`. If a local first inclusion is closed, its paired map is closed
because the product projection is separated; factoring through the closed
graph inclusion proves that `localLift` is closed in `D`. The same
argument proves closedness of `torusLift` from closedness of `i₁`.

For the intended application, take `A j` to be a local Levi subgroup of
`G₁`, `a₁ j` its inclusion, and `a₂ j` a supplied local isomorphism followed
by the corresponding inclusion into `G₂`. Torus compatibility of the local
isomorphisms supplies the hypotheses of `local_torusLift`.

`comparisonIso` constructs the comparison `G₁ ≅ G₂` **conditional on both
projections being isomorphisms**, and `torus_comparisonIso` verifies the
required torus equation. The construction does not establish those
isomorphism hypotheses. It does not construct local Levi isomorphisms,
root factors, rank-one relations, dynamic-factor identifications or density.
The main and Levi gluing isomorphism statements remain unproved by this unit.

The paired-map packaging, the separate common-torus generator and the
all-test compatibility lemmas are internal derived content. The source
motivates the construction; the existence proof and its arbitrary-field
scope come from the imported Library theorem. The official errata snapshot
`milne-2017-algebraic-groups-errata-2026-11-02` has no correction to
23.17–23.18 or printed pp.490–491.
